title: Elm Tree Cabins, Somerville, operated by Frank Seeley
description: In 1919, G. Frank Seeley of Victoria Corner purchased Tom Hurley’s property, located opposite the service station beside the bridge in Hartland. Around 1921, he acquired that service station owned by the Glass Brothers garage and electric power plant, becoming the manager of Hartland Electric Company Ltd. Frank supplied electricity to Hartland, performed electrical wiring, and used a gas engine to generate power. During the Depression years of the 1930s, he operated a second-hand shop in his building, selling bankrupt stock and a variety of old-fashioned goods at remarkably low prices, many of which were still of excellent quality and quite serviceable. In another section of the building, he offered an indoor golf game that was widely patronized. Frank was also an outfitter and, as early as 1932, managed tourist cabins at the top of the bridge hill in Somerville. According to a news clipping, he and his wife, Sadie Clowes, moved to Somerville in 1936 to operate seasonal tourist cabins. Tragically, his home and several cabins were destroyed by fire in 1941.
